no-anaphora.description: Sentences in a row starting with the same word.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A run of sentences that all start with the same word. E5 flags runs of short sentences whatever their first words.

examples.before: Volunteers cleared the trail. Volunteers rebuilt the footbridge. Volunteers repainted the signs.
examples.after: Volunteers cleared the trail and rebuilt the footbridge. They repainted the signs.

what_it_looks_like.example: Marta booked the hall. Marta hired the caterer. Marta printed the badges.

no-anaphora.how_to_fix: Vary the openings so consecutive sentences stop starting with the same word.
no-anaphora.when_to_keep: Deliberate repetition is one of the oldest rhetorical figures in English. Keep a run that builds, contrasts, or intensifies, and keep it in oratory, character voice, or quoted speech. A kept run still flags; the check does not read intent.

editor_guidance.why: Consecutive sentences start with the same word, a mechanical rhythm that reads as filler repetition.
editor_guidance.fix: Vary the openings so consecutive sentences stop starting with the same word.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a run that deliberately builds or intensifies, as in oratory or quoted speech; it stays flagged.

editor_action_policy.reason: Which opener to vary and how depends on rhetorical intent.

no-bland-critical-template.description: Stock criticism phrases that could apply to any review.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Stock evaluative phrases that sound like judgement while saying nothing about a specific scene or sentence.

examples.before: This is the kind of novel that earns its weight through emotional range.
examples.after: The novel needs its length: the narrator grieves her father in one chapter and jokes at his funeral in the next.
fix: grieves her father in one chapter and jokes at his funeral in the next

what_it_looks_like.example: The film is ambitious in an old-fashioned way, with a moral strength that is difficult to dismiss.

no-bland-critical-template.how_to_fix: Replace the phrase with a claim about a specific scene, sentence, or performance.
no-bland-critical-template.when_to_keep: Keep `emotional range` in criticism of acting, where it is literal and the sentence names the emotions a performer plays. That use still counts toward the check.

editor_guidance.why: A stock criticism phrase that fits any book or film stands where a specific judgement should.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the phrase with a claim about a specific scene, sentence, or performance.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep 'emotional range' in criticism of acting when the sentence names the emotions played.

editor_action_policy.reason: The sentence needs a document-specific claim or evaluation.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Bold phrases scattered through ordinary prose. The bolding is mechanical: incidental details get the same emphasis as anything a reader needs to catch.

examples.before: It blends **OKRs**, **KPIs**, and tools such as the **Business Model Canvas** and **Balanced Scorecard**.
examples.after: It blends OKRs, KPIs, and tools such as the Business Model Canvas and Balanced Scorecard.

what_it_looks_like.example: The venue holds **two hundred** people, parking is **free**, doors open at **six**, and the bar is **cash only**.

no-boldface-overuse.how_to_fix: Remove the bold and leave the wording unchanged.
no-boldface-overuse.when_to_keep: Keep bold on a term being defined at its first use, or on the one detail a scanning reader must not miss. Bold in headings and list items is normal formatting.

editor_guidance.why: Bold emphasis runs heavy, so nothing stands out and the page reads as formatted rather than written.
editor_guidance.fix: Remove the bold and leave the wording unchanged.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep bold on a term at its first definition, or on the one detail a scanning reader must not miss.

editor_action_policy.reason: The rate does not determine which emphasis is expendable.

no-collaborative-artifacts.description: AI chat responses addressed to a prompter.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A line from the chat window left in the finished text: a greeting, an offer to help more, a sign-off.

examples.before: I hope this helps! The migration script renames the two legacy columns.
examples.after: The migration script renames the two legacy columns.

what_it_looks_like.example: Let me know if you want me to tighten the middle section.
problem: Let me know if you want me to tighten the middle section

no-collaborative-artifacts.how_to_fix: Cut the line. When it introduces the content instead of giving it, as "here is a summary of" does, replace it with the content itself.
no-collaborative-artifacts.when_to_keep: Keep a line the text quotes and attributes, as when a piece reports what a chatbot said; text inside double quotation marks is not read. In a real letter or newsletter, an invitation such as "let me know if this helps" is the writer speaking to an actual correspondent, and it stays even though the check flags it.

editor_guidance.why: This line addresses the person who asked for the text, not its reader; it is chat residue in finished prose.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the line, or replace an introduction like 'here is a summary of' with the content itself.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep it when quoted and attributed, or when a real letter genuinely speaks to a correspondent.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove a detector-confirmed standalone collaboration residue including owned separators; the author explicitly decides whether the residue is intentional.

no-compound-modifier-density.description: Multiple stock hyphenated phrases in one sentence.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Several of the listed hyphenated phrases packed into one sentence. Each is ordinary English on its own; stacked, they read as marketing copy.

examples.before: The third-party audit praised our data-driven culture and well-defined processes.
examples.after: The outside audit praised our habit of working from data and our clear processes.

what_it_looks_like.example: We need a cost-effective, user-friendly booking page that updates in real-time.

no-compound-modifier-density.how_to_fix: Rewrite the sentence in plain words, keeping only the hyphenated phrases that are genuine terms of art.
no-compound-modifier-density.when_to_keep: Keep a hyphenated phrase that is a genuine term of art with no plain substitute, as `real-time` is in engineering writing; the same phrase laid on as decoration falls under this pattern.

editor_guidance.why: Stock hyphenated modifiers are packed into one sentence, compressing claims into jargon.
editor_guidance.fix: Rewrite the sentence in plain words, keeping only hyphenated phrases that are genuine terms of art.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a phrase that is a genuine term of art with no plain substitute, as 'real-time' in engineering.

editor_action_policy.reason: Unpacking modifiers requires clause and terminology choices.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A hall `serves as` a venue, a town `boasts` three museums. Each verb adds formality without adding a fact, and a page of them reads like brochure copy.

examples.before: Gallery 825 serves as LAAA's exhibition space for contemporary art. The gallery features four separate spaces and boasts over 3,000 square feet.
examples.after: Gallery 825 is LAAA's exhibition space for contemporary art. The gallery has four separate spaces and more than 3,000 square feet.

what_it_looks_like.example: The old mill serves as a community centre for the village.

no-copula-avoidance.how_to_fix: Swap the elaborate verb for the plain one it stands in for: `serves as` becomes `is`, `boasts` and `features` become `has`.
no-copula-avoidance.when_to_keep: Keep the verb when it reports a real stand-in role, as when a sofa serves as a spare bed; there the plain 'is' would claim too much.

editor_guidance.why: An elaborate verb is doing the job of a plain 'is', 'are', or 'has', adding formality without adding a fact.
editor_guidance.fix: Swap the elaborate verb for the plain one: 'serves as' becomes 'is'; 'boasts' and 'features' become 'has'.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the verb when it reports a real stand-in role, as when a sofa serves as a spare bed.

first-sentence-lead.why: The opening sentence introduces its subject with 'refers to' where a plain 'is' would do.
first-sentence-lead.fix: Open with the subject and a plain 'is': 'X refers to a tool' becomes 'X is a tool'.

editor_action_policy.reason: Primary 'features' to 'has'; secondary 'features' to 'includes' for the proven finite-verbal case.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Stock business phrases that describe work without saying what the work was. Each one fits any company and any project.

examples.before: The survey gave us actionable insights into churn.
examples.after: The survey showed us which customers churn and why.

what_it_looks_like.example: Our cross-functional team delivered measurable outcomes this quarter.

no-corporate-ai-speak.how_to_fix: Replace the phrase with the specific project, action, or result it stands for.
no-corporate-ai-speak.when_to_keep: Writing about how teams are organised uses cross-functional as the plain name for a team drawn from several departments. That use still flags; keep it only when the sentence is about team structure itself.

editor_guidance.why: A generic corporate phrase stands in for the specific work it describes.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the phrase with the specific project, action, or result it stands for.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep 'cross-functional' when the sentence is about team structure itself; it still flags.

editor_action_policy.reason: A plain replacement depends on the exact business meaning.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Sentence after sentence says what it was not; the real answer comes last or never. B3 covers the compact `not X; it's Y` reversal; this pattern covers the drawn-out run of denials.

examples.before: It wasn't the venue. It wasn't the catering. It was the date. Half the guests were away that weekend.
examples.after: The date was the problem. Half the guests were away that weekend.

what_it_looks_like.example: It wasn't the salary. It wasn't the hours. It was the commute.

no-countdown-negation.how_to_fix: Cut the negations and say what it was.

editor_guidance.why: Sentence after sentence denies something, a staged countdown rhythm, with or without the final reveal.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the negations and say what it was.

editor_action_policy.reason: A direct rewrite depends on the positive claim and rhetorical structure.

no-curly-quotes.description: Curly quotation marks and apostrophes instead of straight.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Curly quotes and apostrophes where the writer's keyboard would have made straight ones. They arrive through autocorrect or pasting from other software, chat output included.

examples.before: He said “the project is on track” but others disagreed.
examples.after: He said "the project is on track" but others disagreed.

what_it_looks_like.example: We didn’t reach the lighthouse in time.

no-curly-quotes.how_to_fix: Retype the mark as a straight quote or apostrophe.
no-curly-quotes.when_to_keep: Keep curly marks in sourced excerpts, quoted material, and text set for publication, where they are the house style and ordinary typography.

editor_guidance.why: A curly quotation mark or apostrophe sits where the text expects straight ones.
editor_guidance.fix: Retype the mark as a straight quote or apostrophe.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep curly marks in sourced excerpts and text set for publication, where they are house style.

editor_action_policy.reason: Replace each opening or closing curly quote with its straight equivalent.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A stock phrase claims a turning point the events on the page never deliver.

examples.before: I moved my desk next to the kitchen window, and everything changed. I wrote before breakfast instead of after midnight.
examples.after: I moved my desk next to the kitchen window and started writing before breakfast instead of after midnight.
fix: started writing before breakfast instead of after midnight

what_it_looks_like.example: Then the second review came in, and everything changed.

no-dramatic-transitions.how_to_fix: Say what actually changed, or cut the line if nothing did.
no-dramatic-transitions.when_to_keep: Keep the line when the events on the page have earned the turn it announces. The check still flags it there; text inside double quotation marks is not read.

editor_guidance.why: A stock phrase announces a dramatic turn the surrounding text has not built up to.
editor_guidance.fix: Say what actually changed, or cut the line if nothing did.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the line when the events on the page have earned the turn; it stays flagged.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove a detachable standalone transition phrase with its owned punctuation; dramatic pacing may be intentional.

no-em-dashes.description: Use of em dashes in lieu of commas, semicolons, periods, colons, or parentheses.

what_it_looks_like.prose: An em dash standing in for a comma, semicolon, period, or parentheses. Chatbots use it constantly, so routine em dashes read as machine writing.

examples.before: The framework offers a unified approach — one that combines flexibility with rigour.
examples.after: The framework offers a unified approach, one that combines flexibility with rigour.

what_it_looks_like.example: The ferry was late again — the third time this month.

no-em-dashes.how_to_fix: Replace the dash with the mark it stands in for. Between two clauses, use a period or a semicolon. Around an aside, use paired commas or parentheses. Before a list or an explanation, use a colon.
no-em-dashes.when_to_keep: Keep an em dash only when the author deliberately chooses it. The check makes no allowance: it flags a single em dash anywhere, so a kept dash stays flagged.

editor_guidance.why: An em dash is doing the job of a comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses, and routine em dashes read as machine writing.
editor_guidance.fix: What the two halves mean to each other picks the mark: a period or semicolon between clauses, paired commas around an aside, a colon before a list or explanation.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the dash only as a deliberate choice; the check flags every em dash regardless.

editor_action_policy.reason: The right comma, colon, semicolon, parentheses, or sentence split depends on the relationship between the clauses.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Softening phrases repeated until the writing commits to nothing.

examples.before: The new schedule could potentially reduce overtime, and staff tend to prefer the earlier start.
examples.after: The new schedule could reduce overtime, and most staff prefer the earlier start.

what_it_looks_like.example: Broadly speaking, the new roster tends to suit the morning staff.

no-excessive-hedging.how_to_fix:
Cut the hedges and state the claim plainly. Keep one qualifier where the uncertainty is real.

| Phrase | Replacement |
|---|---|
| could potentially | could |
| may possibly | may |
| might conceivably | might |
| generally speaking | usually |
| broadly speaking | mostly |
| it could be argued that | cut |
no-excessive-hedging.when_to_keep: Keep a qualifier that marks real uncertainty, like an early result that later data could overturn. Kept hedges still count toward the check, so writing that leans on many of them still flags.

editor_guidance.why: Impersonal hedge phrases repeat here, and the stacked caution drains the claims.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the hedges and state the claim plainly: 'could potentially' becomes 'could'. Keep one qualifier where the uncertainty is real.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a qualifier that marks real uncertainty, like an early result later data could overturn.

editor_action_policy.reason: Removing a hedge changes epistemic confidence.

no-excessive-lists.description: Overuse of bullets and numbered lists.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Bullet points carry ideas that read better as connected sentences.

examples.before:
The venue works for the launch. A few reasons:

- the room holds eighty people
- parking is free after six
- the caterer is already licensed for the site

We should book it before the March rush.
examples.after: The venue works for the launch: the room holds eighty people, parking is free after six, and the caterer is already licensed for the site. We should book it before the March rush.
problem: - the caterer is already licensed for the site
fix: the room holds eighty people, parking is free after six, and the caterer is already licensed for the site

what_it_looks_like.example:
The trip went well:

- the weather held
- the kids slept in the car
- the cottage had a log fire
problem: - the kids slept in the car
- the cottage had a log fire

no-excessive-lists.how_to_fix: Fold the list back into sentences.
no-excessive-lists.when_to_keep: Keep a list whose items are genuinely separate things: steps, ingredients, parts, specifications. A text built mostly of such lists still flags; keep the lists.

editor_guidance.why: Prose has been converted into bullets and numbered lists beyond what the content needs.
editor_guidance.fix: Fold the list back into sentences.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a list whose items are genuinely separate things: steps, ingredients, parts, specifications.

editor_action_policy.reason: Prose conversion requires grouping and sentence structure choices.

no-false-concession-hedges.description: Avoiding taking positions through concessions and 'both-sides' phrases.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Stock phrases stage a debate or a concession so the writing never takes a position.

examples.before: On the one hand, the new checkout is faster. On the other hand, longtime users dislike the layout.
examples.after: The new checkout is faster, though longtime users dislike the layout.

what_it_looks_like.example: To be fair, there are strong arguments on both sides.

no-false-concession-hedges.how_to_fix: Cut the phrase and state the claim the evidence supports. Keep a real concession as a plain sentence: say what is true and how much it changes the verdict.
no-false-concession-hedges.when_to_keep: Keep a concession that gives ground on something specific, like a review admitting a real flaw before its verdict. The check still flags the phrasing, so a kept concession stays flagged.

editor_guidance.why: Both-sides or concession phrasing is staged here to avoid taking a position.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the phrase and state the claim the evidence supports; give a real concession as a plain sentence.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a concession that gives ground on something specific, like a review admitting a real flaw.

editor_action_policy.reason: Removing the concession can change the argument's epistemic force.

no-false-ranges.description: Sentences with more than one "from X to Y".

what_it_looks_like.prose: Stacked `from X to Y` pairs in one sentence. One pair is ordinary English; a stack claims breadth without saying what is covered.

examples.before: The book takes us from the Big Bang to the cosmic web, from the birth of stars to the dance of dark matter.
examples.after: The book covers the Big Bang, the cosmic web, the birth of stars, and dark matter.
problem: from the Big Bang to the cosmic web
from the birth of stars to the dance of dark matter
fix: covers the Big Bang, the cosmic web, the birth of stars, and dark matter

what_it_looks_like.example: The programme runs from jazz to opera and from talks to films.

no-false-ranges.how_to_fix: Replace the stacked pairs with a plain list of what the passage covers.
no-false-ranges.when_to_keep: Keep a single from-to range. Keep stacked pairs when each one names a literal route or span the sentence reports, as with two legs of a journey.

editor_guidance.why: Stacked from-to pairs gesture at breadth instead of naming what the passage covers.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the stacked pairs with a plain list of what is actually covered.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep pairs that each name a literal route or span the sentence reports, as with two legs of a journey.

editor_action_policy.reason: The actual endpoints or quantifier must come from the author's meaning.

evidence_sources.contribution: The 2026-07-25 corpus calibration measured sentences stacking from-to pairs about five times more often in generated text (0.069 against 0.014 per 1000 words) and single pairs slightly more often in human prose (0.61 against 0.48).

no-filler-phrases.description: Stock padding phrases that do not add anything.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Set phrases stretch the sentence without adding meaning.

examples.before: In order to qualify for the rebate, homeowners must file by June 30.
examples.after: To qualify for the rebate, homeowners must file by June 30.

what_it_looks_like.example: In order to renew your permit, bring both forms to the front desk.

no-filler-phrases.how_to_fix:
Replace the phrase with a word or two, or cut it.

| Phrase | Replacement |
|---|---|
| in order to | to |
| due to the fact that | because |
| at this point in time | now |
| in the event that | if |
| has the ability to | can |
| it is important to note that | cut |
| at the end of the day | cut |
| from a broader perspective | cut |

editor_guidance.why: A stock padding phrase takes up room without adding anything.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the phrase with a word or two, or cut it: 'in order to' becomes 'to', 'due to the fact that' becomes 'because'.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove only whitelisted detachable filler phrases with their owned comma or space; the author decides whether the pacing or stance is deliberate.

no-forced-triads.description: High rate of three-part lists and phrasings.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Lists arriving in threes, again and again through a piece. One triad is ordinary rhetoric; the steady return to three is the tell.

examples.before: The workshop covers planning, drafting, and revision. Each morning begins with a short lecture, a group exercise, and a feedback session, and the afternoons are left open for writing. Participants praised the pace, the setting, and the food, though several asked for more one-on-one time with the tutors. The organisers say next year's programme will add poetry, memoir, and translation strands. Applications open in January and close at the end of February, and the fee covers accommodation, meals, and materials for the full week. Places are limited to twenty, and past attendees get first refusal on the quiet rooms overlooking the orchard.
examples.after: The workshop covers planning and drafting. Each morning begins with a short lecture, a group exercise, and a feedback session, and the afternoons are left open for writing. Participants praised the pace, the setting, and the food, though several asked for more one-on-one time with the tutors. The organisers say next year's programme will add poetry and memoir strands. Applications open in January and close at the end of February, and the fee covers accommodation and meals for the full week. Places are limited to twenty, and past attendees get first refusal on the quiet rooms overlooking the orchard.

what_it_looks_like.example: The night market opened at five, and by six the queue ran past the bank and halfway down the hill. My aunt walked the market rows slowly and filled her string bag with peppers, ginger, and chestnuts. The dumpling stall had sold out before dark, so we queued at the noodle stall instead, where the cook ladled broth, pulled noodles, and shouted orders. Then the rain drove everyone under the awnings, and we stood there in the rain with two farmers, a delivery boy, and a damp terrier. We watched the lanterns swing in the rain until the last tram came up the hill past the bank.
problem: ladled broth, pulled noodles, and shouted orders
two farmers, a delivery boy, and a damp terrier

no-forced-triads.how_to_fix: Cut the item that adds least, so the list runs to two.
no-forced-triads.when_to_keep: Keep a triad that is concrete, necessary, funny, rhythmic, quoted, or deliberately voiced; three-part structures are common in human rhetoric, comedy, fiction, speeches, and criticism. A finding means the cadence repeats through the whole piece.

editor_guidance.why: Three-part lists recur through the piece, and the repeated cadence reads as formula.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the item that adds least so the list runs to two.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a triad that is concrete, funny, rhythmic, or quoted; the finding means the cadence repeats piece-wide.

editor_action_policy.reason: Which item to remove, merge, or expand depends on content.

no-formulaic-openers.description: Stock phrases at the beginning of paragraphs and headings.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Stock templates that start a paragraph and delay its claim. E6 catches connectives anywhere in the text; this pattern covers only a paragraph's first words.

examples.before: At its core, the proposal is about consolidation.
examples.after: The proposal is about consolidation.

what_it_looks_like.example: Moreover, the council never actually voted on the extension.

no-formulaic-openers.how_to_fix: Cut the opener and start with the subject or claim. Replace a vague time frame with the specific year or window.

editor_guidance.why: The paragraph starts with a stock opener template rather than its subject.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the opener and start with the subject or claim; replace a vague time frame with the specific year.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove a detachable opener and separator, preserving the sentence start; the author decides whether the framing is useful.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A stock social-post frame pasted in whole: the plea to save or share, the boast about building something in minutes.

examples.before: I spent 100+ hours so you don't have to. The three note apps differ mainly in how they handle offline edits.
examples.after: I spent over a hundred hours on this comparison. The three note apps differ mainly in how they handle offline edits.
problem: I spent 100+ hours so you don't have to
fix: I spent over a hundred hours on this comparison

what_it_looks_like.example: I built this in 20 minutes with a spreadsheet and one free plugin.
problem: I built this in 20 minutes with a spreadsheet and one free plugin

no-formulaic-social-posts.how_to_fix: Cut the frame and state the actual request, experience, or result directly.
no-formulaic-social-posts.when_to_keep: Keep a quoted specimen: a piece about these formulas shows one to report the frame, and text inside double quotation marks is not read.

editor_guidance.why: This is a ready-made social post formula; the frame writes the post before the content does.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the frame and state the actual request, experience, or result directly.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a quoted specimen in a piece about these formulas; quoted text is not read.

editor_action_policy.reason: The whole frame and voice need rewriting; deletion can remove necessary content.

what_it_looks_like.prose: The piece ends on an upbeat line that says nothing specific about the subject.

examples.before: The bakery will add a second oven in March. The future looks bright, and exciting times lie ahead.
examples.after: The bakery will add a second oven in March and hire two weekend staff.

what_it_looks_like.example: With two new sponsors signed, the future looks bright for the club.

no-generic-conclusions.how_to_fix: End on a specific fact or expectation about the subject. If the piece has made its point, cut the ending and stop.

editor_guidance.why: The ending is vague enough to close any article on any topic.
editor_guidance.fix: End on a specific fact or expectation about the subject; if the piece has already made its point, cut the ending and stop.

short-exclamatory-final.why: The piece signs off on a short exclamatory cheer rather than a claim about the subject.
short-exclamatory-final.fix: Cut the cheer; end on the last real point.

editor_action_policy.reason: The conclusion must be replaced with the document's actual implication.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Spectral imagery laid on to make a subject feel deep: shadows, whispers, echoes, ghosts. One image is a choice; the same imagery again and again is the tell.

examples.before: The cottage still holds the ghosts of its former tenants. Shadows gather in the stairwell, and every draught carries a whisper of the past.
examples.after: The cottage has had no tenants for decades. The stairwell is dark and the building is draughty.
fix: has had no tenants for decades

what_it_looks_like.example: The old platform still carries echoes of the steam era, with deep shadows under the footbridge and a lingering smell of coal.

no-ghost-spectral-density.how_to_fix: Replace each spectral image with what is literally there.
no-ghost-spectral-density.when_to_keep: Keep the words where they are literal: a piece about a ghost story, a shadow across a doorway, or a real echo in a stairwell needs them. The check counts literal uses the same as decorative ones, so a piece that keeps enough of them still flags; treat the flag as a prompt to confirm each use is literal.

editor_guidance.why: Ghostly and spectral words recur as decoration, a stock atmosphere machine prose reaches for.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace each spectral image with what is literally there.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep words that are literal, as in a real ghost story or an actual echo; confirm each use is literal.

editor_action_policy.reason: Which atmospheric word to retain depends on the scene.

no-heading-one-liners.description: Repeated headings followed by a single sentence.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A heading, one sentence, then the next heading, repeated down the page. The piece reads as an outline that never got filled in.

examples.before:
## Refunds

Refunds go back to the original card within five days.

## Exchanges

Exchanges are posted free within Australia.
examples.after: Refunds go back to the original card within five days, and exchanges are posted free within Australia.
fix: Refunds go back to the original card within five days, and exchanges are posted free within Australia

what_it_looks_like.example:
## Parking

The lot behind the library is free after six.

## Tickets

Door sales are cash only.

no-heading-one-liners.how_to_fix: Develop the section with real content, or fold its one sentence into surrounding prose and drop the heading.
no-heading-one-liners.when_to_keep: Keep the shape in a glossary where each heading names a term and one sentence defines it. The check still flags it there.

editor_guidance.why: A heading introduces a section of just one sentence, so the structure outweighs the content.
editor_guidance.fix: If the section has more to say, develop it; if not, fold its one sentence into surrounding prose and drop the heading.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the shape in a glossary, where a heading names a term and one sentence defines it.

editor_action_policy.reason: Expanding, merging, or removing the section depends on its role.

no-inline-header-lists.description: List items that start with a bold label and a colon, or several bold labels on one line.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Bullets where a bold label announces the topic and the sentence restates it. The reader gets every idea twice. When pasting strips the bullets, the labels run together on one line.

examples.before:
- **Performance:** Performance has been enhanced through optimised algorithms.
- **Security:** Security has been strengthened with end-to-end encryption.
examples.after: The update improves performance with optimised algorithms and strengthens security with end-to-end encryption.

what_it_looks_like.example:
- **Location:** The venue is located in the Corn Exchange.
- **Price:** Tickets are priced at twelve pounds.

no-inline-header-lists.how_to_fix: Fold each labelled bullet into a plain prose sentence and drop the label.
no-inline-header-lists.when_to_keep: Keep the format in a genuine spec or reference list, where each label names a field and what follows it is the field's value.

editor_guidance.why: List items open with a bold label and colon, imposing a spec format on prose content.
editor_guidance.fix: Fold each labelled bullet into a plain prose sentence and drop the label.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the format in a genuine spec or reference list, where each label names a field.

editor_action_policy.reason: Restructuring requires choosing heading, prose, or list semantics.

no-knowledge-cutoff-disclaimers.description: Disclaimers of knowledge limitations or training data.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A chatbot's disclaimer about its own knowledge left in the text: details are scarce, nothing had changed as of some update. D1 covers leftover chat lines; this pattern covers hedges attached to facts.

examples.before: While specific details are not extensively documented in readily available sources, the company appears to have been founded in the 1990s.
examples.after: The company was founded in 1994.
problem: While specific details are not extensively documented in readily available sources
appears to have been founded in the 1990s

what_it_looks_like.example: As of my last update, the branch on Harper Street had not reopened.

no-knowledge-cutoff-disclaimers.how_to_fix: Find the missing fact and state it, or cut the disclaimer.
no-knowledge-cutoff-disclaimers.when_to_keep: Keep the phrase when a real correspondent is speaking, as in a letter that tells a customer "I am unable to confirm your booking"; the check still flags it. A piece that reports a model's disclaimer keeps the quote, and text inside double quotation marks is not read.

editor_guidance.why: A chatbot's disclaimer about its own knowledge is left in the text, speaking as the machine, not the writer.
editor_guidance.fix: Find the missing fact and state it; if the piece does not need the fact, cut the disclaimer.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep it when a real correspondent is speaking, as in a letter to a customer; quoted disclaimers are not read.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove a detector-confirmed standalone disclaimer sentence and owned following separator; the author decides whether the limitation is materially required.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Stock phrases stage a revelation the sentence never delivers. B3 covers the contrast shape; this pattern covers the reveal wording.

examples.before: What nobody is talking about is the maintenance backlog. The bridge inspection found forty cracked bearings.
examples.after: The maintenance backlog is the issue. The bridge inspection found forty cracked bearings.
fix: The maintenance backlog is the issue

what_it_looks_like.example: Here's the thing: the budget was never the real problem.

no-manufactured-insight.how_to_fix: Drop the framing and state the claim plainly, or cut the line if there is no claim underneath. A phrase like `What nobody is talking about` claims a real silence; back the claim or cut it.
no-manufactured-insight.when_to_keep: Text inside double quotation marks is not read, so a quoted saying never flags. A plain factual sentence that happens to fit an aphorism shape, such as naming someone the head of a team, still flags; keep it as written.

editor_guidance.why: A stock frame stages this line as a revelation the text has not earned.
editor_guidance.fix: Drop the framing and state the claim plainly, or cut the line if no claim sits underneath.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a plain factual sentence that merely fits an aphorism shape; quoted sayings are not read.

editor_action_policy.reason: Replacing the frame requires the actual claim or evidence.

no-mixed-spelling-conventions.description: British and American spellings of the same word families.

what_it_looks_like.prose: An `organised` in one paragraph, a `recognized` in the next. A person settles into one convention; machine text drifts between the two.

examples.before: The council organised the review in March. By June the department had recognized that the timetable would not hold.
examples.after: The council organised the review in March. By June the department had recognised that the timetable would not hold.

what_it_looks_like.example: The organizers repainted the harbour railings a week before the show.

no-mixed-spelling-conventions.how_to_fix: Respell the stray word in the convention the rest of the text already uses.
no-mixed-spelling-conventions.when_to_keep: Keep a spelling that belongs to a proper name, such as the Department of Defense or the Australian Labor Party in a British text. Quoted material also keeps its source's spelling.

editor_guidance.why: British and American spellings of the same word families share this text, so no single voice holds.
editor_guidance.fix: Respell the stray word in the convention the rest of the text already uses.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a spelling that belongs to a proper name or quoted material; those keep their source's convention.

editor_action_policy.reason: Primary replaces with the document's established convention; secondary offers the mapped alternative, because the author may intentionally preserve a quoted or house style.

no-modal-stacks.description: Multiple qualifying words in a sentence.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Several softening qualifiers stack in one sentence until no firm claim is left. E2 counts hedges across the whole text; this pattern flags one overloaded sentence.

examples.before: The new cache can potentially reduce latency, and typically helps most tenants.
examples.after: The new cache typically reduces latency for most tenants.

what_it_looks_like.example: Cold starts can sometimes take longer, and older phones might struggle.

no-modal-stacks.how_to_fix: Keep the one qualifier the claim needs and delete the rest.

editor_guidance.why: Several softening qualifiers are stacked in one sentence, so the claim barely commits to anything.
editor_guidance.fix: Keep the one qualifier the claim needs and delete the rest.

editor_action_policy.reason: Removing a qualifier changes confidence and obligation.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Sentence after sentence saying what things are not. H1 flags a few negations in a row; this pattern flags a whole text that leans on them.

examples.before: The new intake process isn't complicated, but the guide doesn't explain it. The first page isn't a form; it is a checklist, and the checklist isn't optional. Referrals don't go to the duty desk any more, and the desk isn't staffed on Mondays anyway. The old fax number doesn't work, the scanner isn't connected, and the shared inbox isn't monitored after five. Applicants aren't told any of this, and their files don't move until someone notices. The delays aren't the staff's fault, and they aren't the applicants' fault either.
examples.after: The new intake process is simple, but the guide leaves it unexplained. The first page is a checklist rather than a form, and the checklist is mandatory. Referrals now skip the duty desk, which sits empty on Mondays anyway. The old fax number is dead, the scanner sits unplugged, and the shared inbox goes unread after five. Applicants discover all of this at the counter, and their files sit still until someone notices. The delays come from the process itself.
fix: is a checklist rather than a form
discover all of this at the counter

what_it_looks_like.example: The new booking form isn't an improvement, and the help page doesn't explain the deposit rules, which weren't a problem on the old form. The weekend times aren't right either, because the calendar doesn't know about the summer schedule. Refunds aren't automatic, the money doesn't come back for a fortnight, and the confirmation email doesn't say so. The phone line isn't staffed after four, the office isn't open on Fridays, and the voicemail box wasn't emptied once all summer. I don't think anyone tested the new form with real members.

no-negation-density.how_to_fix: Rewrite each sentence to say what the thing is. Keep a denial only where it answers a real claim.
no-negation-density.when_to_keep: Keep dense negation in a rebuttal that answers claims point by point; there, saying what is not true is the work. A long rebuttal still flags.

editor_guidance.why: Negations run dense here, so the text keeps saying what things are not.
editor_guidance.fix: Rewrite each sentence to say what the thing is; keep a denial only where it answers a real claim.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep dense negation in a rebuttal that answers claims point by point; it still flags.

editor_action_policy.reason: Positive recasting changes sentence structure and emphasis.

no-negative-parallelisms.description: Negative parallelisms like "It's not X, it's Y" and its variants.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A sentence that says what something is not, then what it is: `It's not X, it's Y`. Splitting the turn across two sentences is the same pattern.

examples.before: It's not just about the beat riding under the vocals; it's part of the aggression and atmosphere.
examples.after: The heavy beat adds to the aggressive tone throughout the track.

what_it_looks_like.example: The delay isn't a scheduling problem; it's a staffing problem.
problem: isn't a scheduling problem; it's a staffing problem

no-negative-parallelisms.how_to_fix: State the point directly: keep the half of the contrast that carries it and cut the denial. `It's not the money, it's the time` becomes `The time is the problem`.
no-negative-parallelisms.when_to_keep: Keep a reversal that corrects something the reader really believes, because there the denial does real work. A plain 'rather than' weighing two genuine options is ordinary English.

editor_guidance.why: The point is built by reversal, not X but Y, a contrast structure machine writing overuses.
editor_guidance.fix: Keep the half of the contrast that carries the point and cut the denial: 'It's not the money, it's the time' becomes 'The time is the problem'.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a reversal that corrects something the reader really believes; there the denial does real work.

editor_action_policy.reason: A direct positive sentence depends on the intended contrast.

no-nonliteral-land-surface.description: Abstract concepts described as navigation or geography terms.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Arguments `land`, plans become `roadmaps`: a physical word stands in for the action or claim the writer never states.

examples.before: The budget question surfaces in the discussion near the end of the call.
examples.after: Dana raises the budget question near the end of the call.

what_it_looks_like.example: The argument lands somewhere between optimism and despair.

no-nonliteral-land-surface.how_to_fix: Replace the figurative phrase with the concrete action or claim it stands for.
no-nonliteral-land-surface.when_to_keep: A joke or a line landing with a real audience is ordinary performance idiom. That use still flags; keep it when an actual audience was there to react.

editor_guidance.why: An abstract thing is described as landing or surfacing, or a plan recast as a roadmap; the figure blurs what actually happened.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the figurative phrase with the concrete action or claim it stands for.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the idiom for a joke or line landing when a real audience was there to react.

editor_action_policy.reason: The literal subject and verb must come from author intent.

no-notability-claims.description: Vague claims of press coverage or popularity.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Names press coverage or a following as proof the subject matters, without saying what any outlet said.

examples.before: Her views have been cited in The New York Times, BBC, and the Financial Times.
examples.after: In a 2024 New York Times interview, she argued that regulators should judge AI systems by their outcomes.
problem: cited in The New York Times, BBC, and the Financial Times
fix: she argued that regulators should judge AI systems by their outcomes

what_it_looks_like.example: The bakery was profiled in two food magazines last spring.

no-notability-claims.how_to_fix: Name the outlet, what it said, and when, or cut the claim.
no-notability-claims.when_to_keep: Keep it when the sentence says who covered it, what they said, and when, or gives a real count with a date, like "her channel passed half a million subscribers in March".

editor_guidance.why: The sentence claims coverage or popularity without saying what any outlet said.
editor_guidance.fix: Name the outlet, what it said, and when; without those specifics, cut the claim.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep it when the sentence names who covered it and what they said, or gives a real count with a date.

editor_action_policy.reason: A supported rewrite requires actual evidence of notability.

evidence_sources.contribution: Catalogues notability-claim framing, including asserted media coverage and social-media presence, among editor-observed signs in AI-written Wikipedia articles.
A practitioner rewriting guide that names this pattern and shows before and after fixes.

no-orphaned-demonstratives.description: Starting sentences with 'This' or 'That' with no noun after it.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A bare `this` or `that` as the subject leaves the reader guessing what it points at. H5 covers runs of sentences starting with `This`; this pattern covers vague `this` and `that` subjects anywhere in the text.

examples.before: The store ran the promotion for two weeks, and sales rose only in the final days. This suggests shoppers waited for the deeper cuts. Returns climbed over the same stretch. Taken together, that shows the staggered discounts confused people, and this underscores the case for one flat price.
examples.after: The store ran the promotion for two weeks, and sales rose only in the final days. The late surge suggests shoppers waited for the deeper cuts. Returns climbed over the same stretch. Together, the surge and the returns show the staggered discounts confused people and argue for one flat price.

what_it_looks_like.example: The seal was worn, the gauge read low, and the log skipped a week. This suggests the fault sat unnoticed for a while. The crew found rust on the intake too, and that points to water in the line. Put together, this shows the maintenance schedule failed.

no-orphaned-demonstratives.how_to_fix: Replace the bare `this` or `that` with the noun or claim it points to.
no-orphaned-demonstratives.when_to_keep: Keep a `this` or `that` that points at one clear thing named just before it. A kept one still counts toward the check's total.

editor_guidance.why: A bare 'this' or 'that' points at a whole passage instead of one nameable thing, so the reader has to guess.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the bare 'this' or 'that' with the noun or claim it points to.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep one that points at a single clear thing named just before it; it still counts toward the total.

editor_action_policy.reason: The missing noun or referent must come from the author.

no-paragraph-anaphora.description: Paragraphs in a row starting with the same word.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A run of paragraphs that all start with the same word. H14 covers repeated sentence starts; this pattern covers repeated paragraph starts.

examples.before:
Customers want faster onboarding.

Customers expect clean invoice exports.

Customers who churn cite support gaps.
examples.after:
Customers want faster onboarding.

They expect clean invoice exports.

The ones who churn cite support gaps.

what_it_looks_like.example:
Rehearsals start at six on Mondays.

Rehearsals move to the annex in July.

Rehearsals before a concert run long.

no-paragraph-anaphora.how_to_fix: Reword the openings so each paragraph starts with a different word.
no-paragraph-anaphora.when_to_keep: Deliberate repetition is a real device: a speech or a manifesto starts each paragraph the same way on purpose. The check still flags the run; keep it when each repeat says more than the last.

editor_guidance.why: Consecutive paragraphs open with the same word, which reads as template structure.
editor_guidance.fix: Reword the openings so each paragraph starts with a different word.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep it in a speech or manifesto where each repeat says more than the last; the run stays flagged.

editor_action_policy.reason: Paragraph openings require content-aware restructuring.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A heading carrying a parenthetical aside. The qualifier or side comment stops the heading being a plain name for its section.

examples.before: ## Document skills (the steady ones)
examples.after:
## Document skills

These are the steady ones.

what_it_looks_like.example: ## Venue Options (Shortlist)

no-parenthetical-headings.how_to_fix: Rewrite the heading as a plain label and move the aside into the body.

editor_guidance.why: The heading carries a parenthetical aside, doing body-text work in a label.
editor_guidance.fix: Rewrite the heading as a plain label and move the aside into the body.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove only the wrapping parentheses from a complete heading.

no-performed-candour.description: Announcements of the writer's honesty, bravery, or expected backlash placed in front of a claim.

what_it_looks_like.prose: The writer declares honesty or bravery before making the claim. The declaration performs sincerity; the claim means the same without it.

examples.before: To be honest, the review process is too slow.
examples.after: The review process is too slow.

what_it_looks_like.example: I'll be honest: the second act still drags.

no-performed-candour.when_to_keep: A reply to someone who asked for honesty uses the phrase literally: the question was about candour, so the answer names it. That use still flags; keep it when the request for honesty is on the page.

editor_guidance.why: The line announces honesty, bravery, or expected backlash before the claim, performing candour instead of showing it.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the announcement and let the claim stand on its own.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep it when a request for honesty is on the page and the reply names candour literally.

editor_action_policy.reason: Whether to state, qualify, or remove the admission depends on intended stance.

no-placeholder-residue.description: Unfilled templates, leftover instructions and markup.

what_it_looks_like.prose: One unfilled template slot, drafting instruction, or piece of stray markup proves nobody gave the text a final read.

examples.before: Hi {customer_name}, your March invoice is attached.
examples.after: Hi Priya, your March invoice is attached.

what_it_looks_like.example: Dear [Name], thank you for your order.

no-placeholder-residue.how_to_fix: Fill the slot with the real value. Cut drafting instructions and stray markup once anything they asked for is done.
no-placeholder-residue.when_to_keep: Writing that teaches templating shows its slots on purpose: instructions for a mail-merge letter need `{first_name}` where the name will go. The check flags a kept slot all the same.

editor_guidance.why: An unfilled template slot, drafting instruction, or stray platform markup is left in finished text.
editor_guidance.fix: Fill the slot with the real value; cut drafting instructions and stray markup once their job is done.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a slot that teaching material shows on purpose, as in mail-merge instructions.

editor_action_policy.reason: Policy differs by residue case: template slot, platform residue, and drafting instruction each carry their own decided action.

template-slot.reason: A template slot needs an author-supplied value.

platform-residue.reason: Proven platform residue may be removed.

drafting-instruction.reason: Drafting instructions may be removed only by explicit author choice.

no-promotional-language.description: Stock hype words and motivational slogans.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Reads like tourism marketing.

examples.before: Nestled in the breathtaking Gonder region of Ethiopia, Alamata Raya Kobo is a town with a rich cultural heritage and stunning natural beauty.
examples.after: Alamata Raya Kobo is a town in northern Ethiopia.

what_it_looks_like.example: The inn is nestled at the foot of the pass.

no-promotional-language.how_to_fix: Cut the hype word or replace it with the specific detail that backs the claim.
no-promotional-language.when_to_keep: Keep quoted marketing copy and enthusiasm voiced by a named speaker. Keep a listed word when it means the thing literally: a "groundbreaking" ceremony breaks real ground, and "profound" hearing loss is a medical description.

editor_guidance.why: A stock hype word makes the sentence read like sales copy instead of description.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the hype word with the specific detail that backs the claim, or cut it when no detail backs it.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep quoted marketing, a named speaker's enthusiasm, or a literal use like a groundbreaking ceremony.

editor_action_policy.reason: A neutral replacement depends on the underlying factual claim.

evidence_sources.contribution: Catalogues promotional language among editor-observed signs in AI-written Wikipedia articles.
Lists seven buzzword hype terms among 31 words and phrases it associates with AI-generated prose and supplies plainer replacements.
Names a specific set of promotional phrases as a sign of AI writing; part of that set is in this check's watch list.
Names inflated hype and cliche slogan formulas as the first sign of AI-written marketing email, with seven quoted slogan examples.

no-quietness-obsession.description: High rate of words relating to quiet or softness.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A mood of quiet laid over the scene: everything turns quiet, soft, gentle, and still, whatever is actually there.

examples.before: The library reading room settled into a quiet rhythm by mid-morning. Pages turned softly and chairs shifted with gentle scrapes.
examples.after: By mid-morning the only sounds in the reading room were pages turning and the scrape of chairs.

what_it_looks_like.example: The company's quiet exit from the tablet market was a gentle winding down: updates softly stopped and the product page settled into stillness.

no-quietness-obsession.how_to_fix: Cut the quietness word, or replace it with the specific detail the scene contains.
no-quietness-obsession.when_to_keep: Keep a word that is doing literal work: a hospital ward at night is quiet, bread dough is soft, a dispute gets settled. The check counts these uses the same as mood-setting ones, so a piece that keeps enough of them still flags; confirm each use is literal before letting it stand.

editor_guidance.why: Words of quiet and softness recur as mood-setting, a default atmosphere in machine prose.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the quietness word with the specific detail the scene contains, or cut it when the scene has none.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a word doing literal work: a ward at night is quiet, bread dough is soft.

editor_action_policy.reason: Which quietness cue to retain depends on pacing and scene intent.

no-rhetorical-questions.description: Short fragmented questions immediately answered by the next sentence.

what_it_looks_like.prose: The writing splits a statement into a mock question and its answer. The beat imitates spoken emphasis.

examples.before: The result? It's simpler than you think.
examples.after: The result is simpler than you think.

what_it_looks_like.example: The verdict? Worth every penny.

no-rhetorical-questions.how_to_fix: Rewrite the fragment and its answer as one direct statement.
no-rhetorical-questions.when_to_keep: Keep a short question-and-answer beat that reproduces real speech, as in an interview transcript. The check still flags it there; keep the line as spoken.

editor_guidance.why: A short fragment is punctuated as a question with its answer straight after, a staged beat.
editor_guidance.fix: Rewrite the fragment and its answer as one direct statement.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a question-and-answer beat that reproduces real speech, as in an interview transcript.

editor_action_policy.reason: Converting a question to a statement requires the intended answer or claim.

no-rubric-echoing.description: Inappropriate references to assignment grading or rubrics.

what_it_looks_like.prose: The essay repeats the assignment's wording instead of making its own claims about the text. Machine-written schoolwork mirrors the prompt it was given.

examples.before: In paragraph three, the author creates a mournful tone. This quote shows that the narrator misses her sister.
examples.after: The third paragraph is mournful: the narrator's own words make plain that she misses her sister.
problem: the author creates a mournful tone
fix: the narrator's own words make plain

what_it_looks_like.example: In paragraph two, the author creates a hopeful tone. I can tell because the ending is uplifting.
problem: the author creates a hopeful tone

no-rubric-echoing.how_to_fix: Rewrite the sentence as a direct claim about the text. Leave the assignment's wording out.
no-rubric-echoing.when_to_keep: Writing that is actually about an assignment or its marking, such as guidance for teachers, uses rubric language as its subject. Those uses still count toward the check; text inside double quotation marks is not read.

editor_guidance.why: The sentence echoes assignment or grading-rubric wording instead of making a claim about the text.
editor_guidance.fix: Rewrite the sentence as a direct claim about the text; leave the assignment's wording out.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep rubric language when the writing is actually about an assignment or its marking.

editor_action_policy.reason: The rewrite must answer the task rather than paraphrase its rubric.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A short label repeated above every section, or mechanical heading structure: a divider line right before a heading, a first heading set too deep, or a skipped heading level.

examples.before:
1. Build trust early
How to make this work:
Start with small wins.

2. Communicate clearly
How to make this work:
Hold regular standups.

3. Measure outcomes
How to make this work:
Define success metrics before you start tracking.
examples.after:
1. Build trust early
Start with small wins.

2. Communicate clearly
Hold regular standups.

3. Measure outcomes
Define success metrics before you start tracking.

what_it_looks_like.example:
The venue list is final.

---

## Catering

Quotes are due Friday.

no-section-scaffolding.how_to_fix: Cut the repeated label, delete the divider before the heading, or move the heading to its proper level.
no-section-scaffolding.when_to_keep: Formats that are templates on purpose repeat short labels by design: a glossary, a question and answer page, or a transcript with speaker names on their own lines. The check still flags them; keep the repetition when the format calls for it.

editor_guidance.why: The document's structural chrome shows: a repeated label, a skipped heading level, or a divider before a heading.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the repeated label, delete the divider before the heading, or move the heading to its proper level.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep deliberate template repetition, as in a glossary, question-and-answer page, or transcript.

editor_action_policy.reason: Removing or merging a section depends on document structure.

no-significance-inflation.description: Inflating the importance of topics to historic.

what_it_looks_like.prose: An ordinary fact written up as a historic moment: it `marks a pivotal moment` or `stands as a testament`, with no reason given why it matters.

examples.before: The Statistical Institute of Catalonia was established in 1989, marking a pivotal moment in the evolution of regional statistics in Spain.
examples.after: The Statistical Institute of Catalonia was established in 1989.
problem: marking a pivotal moment in the evolution of regional statistics in Spain

what_it_looks_like.example: The win was a testament to a season of early-morning training.

no-significance-inflation.how_to_fix:
Replace the frame with the plain verb that names what happened, or cut it when the sentence already makes the point.

| Phrase | Replacement |
|---|---|
| stands as a testament to | shows |
| marks a pivotal moment in | changed |
| plays a crucial role in | helps |
| represents a shift | changed |
| a key turning point | changed |
| reflects a broader trend | is part of |
| sets the stage for | came before |
| paves the way for | led to |
| has left an indelible mark | shaped |
| the evolving landscape of | the field |
| deeply rooted | long-standing |
no-significance-inflation.when_to_keep: Keep the frame when the source itself argues significance, a named historian or critic does the arguing, and the text attributes the claim.

editor_guidance.why: The frame inflates an ordinary fact into a historic moment.
editor_guidance.fix: Replace the frame with the plain verb that names what happened: 'stands as a testament to' becomes 'shows'.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the frame when a named historian or critic argues the significance and the text attributes it.

editor_action_policy.reason: The warranted level of significance depends on evidence.

evidence_sources.contribution: Found 21 words, including forms of underscore, used far more often in GPT-3.5 science summaries and rising sharply in published summaries after 2022.
Counted word use in 15.1 million medical paper summaries; the words that spiked in 2024 were style words, and at least 13.5 percent of 2024 summaries showed LLM help.
Publishes 100 phrases ranked by AI-to-human ratio from 3.3 million texts, several of which overlap significance and importance language.
Lists pivotal and underscores the importance of among 31 words and phrases it associates with AI-generated prose.
Shows early chatbot prose claiming importance it never earns.
Lists exact promotional phrases as a sign of LLM writing; part of that list is in this check's watch list.
Catalogues significance and importance inflation among editor-observed signs in AI-written Wikipedia articles.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A label announces the conclusion: a closing paragraph that starts with `In conclusion`, or a heading that names the wrap-up.

examples.before: In conclusion, the pilot cut the reporting backlog in half.
examples.after: The pilot cut the reporting backlog in half.

what_it_looks_like.example: In conclusion, the trial went well.

no-signposted-conclusions.how_to_fix: Cut the signpost and let the final paragraph stand on its own. Delete a heading like `Conclusion` or `Final thoughts` the same way.
no-signposted-conclusions.when_to_keep: Keep a flagged Conclusion heading when the format calls for it, as in formal reports, academic papers, and structured policy briefs.

editor_guidance.why: A label announces that the conclusion is coming instead of letting it arrive.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the signpost, and delete a heading like 'Conclusion' the same way; let the final paragraph stand.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a Conclusion heading where the format calls for it, as in formal reports and academic papers.

editor_action_policy.reason: Remove an exact standalone conclusion marker while preserving its section content; explicit signposting may be appropriate.

no-soft-scaffolding.description: Bland connective phrases without a point.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Bland phrases that announce where a point sits instead of making it. E1 catches stock padding; this pattern catches the connectives between points.

examples.before: One useful area is structuring feedback. Another useful area is timing it well.
examples.after: Structure the feedback and time it well.

what_it_looks_like.example: One useful habit is reading the minutes before the meeting. Another useful habit is writing the summary the same day.

no-soft-scaffolding.how_to_fix: Cut the phrase and state the point directly.

editor_guidance.why: The phrase announces where a point sits in the structure instead of making the point.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the phrase and state the point directly.

editor_action_policy.reason: A direct transition depends on the next claim and section structure.

no-staccato-sequences.description: Short sentences used for dramatic emphasis.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Short sentences fired in a row so the rhythm supplies the emphasis. Machine text falls into this beat on any subject, however plain the news.

examples.before: Support tickets doubled. Nobody escalated. The dashboard stayed green. By Friday the on-call engineer found the failed migration.
examples.after: Support tickets doubled, nobody escalated, and the dashboard stayed green. By Friday the on-call engineer found the failed migration.
fix: Support tickets doubled, nobody escalated, and the dashboard stayed green

what_it_looks_like.example: We counted the boxes again. Twelve were still missing. Nobody had signed anything.

no-staccato-sequences.how_to_fix: Merge the short sentences into longer ones of varied length. Cut a bare fragment like `Full stop.` outright.
no-staccato-sequences.when_to_keep: Keep the rhythm when it is character voice, panic, comedy, dialogue, aphorism, or deliberate literary style; the check still flags it.

editor_guidance.why: Very short sentences are doing emphasis work here, a rhythm machine writing leans on.
editor_guidance.fix: Merge the short sentences into longer ones of varied length; cut a bare fragment outright.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the rhythm for character voice, panic, comedy, or dialogue; the check still flags it.

staccato-short-sentence-run.why: A run of {runLength} short sentences lands here as staged emphasis.

staccato-repeated-opener-run.fix: Vary the repeated {opener} openings and fold some of the short sentences together.

staccato-dramatic-formula.fix: Cut the dramatic fragment or fold it into the sentence before it.

staccato-short-sentence-rate.why: Short sentences make up an outsized share of the whole piece, not just one run.
staccato-short-sentence-rate.fix: Lengthen or merge short sentences across the piece until the rhythm varies.

staccato-mean-sentence-length.why: The average sentence here runs very short across the whole piece.
staccato-mean-sentence-length.fix: Combine related sentences so the average length rises and varies.

editor_action_policy.reason: Merging sentences requires choosing conjunction, subordination, and emphasis.

no-superficial-ing.description: Sentences starting with a gerund-participle (an '-ing' word), or commas followed by a participle that claims meaning, emphasis or causation.

what_it_looks_like.prose: A sentence that starts with an `-ing` phrase, or tacks one on after a comma to say what the fact shows or means.

examples.before: Rising above the plaza, the temple pairs blue and green tile, symbolizing the region's bluebonnets and the Gulf coast.
examples.after: The temple rises above the plaza and pairs blue and green tile. The colours echo the region's bluebonnets and the Gulf coast.
problem: symbolizing the region's bluebonnets and the Gulf coast
fix: The temple rises above the plaza

what_it_looks_like.example: Attendance doubled in the second year, reflecting the switch to free entry.
problem: reflecting the switch to free entry

no-superficial-ing.how_to_fix: Rewrite the clause as its own sentence. If it claims a meaning or cause, name it or cut it.

editor_guidance.why: An '-ing' clause opens the sentence, or trails after a comma to claim what something means, shows, or achieves, without arguing it.
editor_guidance.fix: Rewrite the clause as its own sentence; if it claims a meaning or cause, name it or cut it.

editor_action_policy.reason: A finite-clause rewrite requires subject, tense, and causal relation.

evidence_sources.contribution: Reports AI-assisted student papers tacking generic meaning onto sentences in trailing -ing clauses, including a symbolizing example this check catches.
Catalogues superficial trailing analysis clauses among editor-observed signs in AI-written Wikipedia articles.
Finds AI opens sentences with -ing phrases two to five times as often as human writers.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Every item in the list runs to the same length and starts or ends with the same word. The list reads as one template filled in several times.

examples.before:
- Faster load times for dashboard users
- Simpler login flow for mobile users
- Clearer error messages for API users
examples.after:
- Dashboard load times are faster
- Logging in on mobile is simpler
- The error messages the API returns are clearer

what_it_looks_like.example:
The launch post promises:

- Empowering teams to ship faster
- Empowering managers to plan smarter
- Empowering leaders to see further

no-symmetric-list-items.how_to_fix: Let each item take the length and shape its content needs.
no-symmetric-list-items.when_to_keep: Keep the symmetry in specifications, comparison entries, and reference lists, where every item answers the same question in the same form. The check still flags them.

editor_guidance.why: The list items are held to the same length and share a first or last word, a symmetry that reads as generated.
editor_guidance.fix: Let each item take the length and shape its content needs.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the symmetry in specifications and reference lists, where every item answers the same question.

editor_action_policy.reason: Breaking symmetry requires content-aware variation.

no-this-chains.description: Sequential sentences starting with "This" and a verb.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Sentence after sentence starts with `This` plus a verb, so the paragraph never names its own subject. H4 covers vague `this` subjects anywhere in the text; this pattern covers consecutive sentences starting with `This`.

examples.before: The framework launched in March. This brought consolidation. This reduced cost. This freed engineering time.
examples.after: The framework launched in March. The consolidation it brought reduced cost and freed engineering time.

what_it_looks_like.example: This cuts the export time. This spares the interns. This keeps the auditors happy.

no-this-chains.how_to_fix: Give each sentence its real subject: name the thing `This` stands for.

editor_guidance.why: Consecutive sentences start with 'This' plus a verb, so each leans on the last instead of naming its subject.
editor_guidance.fix: Give each sentence its real subject: name the thing 'This' stands for.

editor_action_policy.reason: Each 'This' needs a context-specific noun or referent.

what_it_looks_like.prose: The last sentence of each paragraph restates the point just made or announces the next topic.

examples.before: The survey went out in March and closed in June. Response rates were highest in the north. That is why the follow-up interviews started there.
examples.after: The survey went out in March and closed in June. Response rates were highest in the north, so the follow-up interviews started there.
problem: That is why the follow-up interviews started there
fix: so the follow-up interviews started there

what_it_looks_like.example: The council rejected both bids on cost. That is why the tender went elsewhere.
problem: That is why the tender went elsewhere

no-tidy-paragraph-endings.how_to_fix: Cut the closing summary. If it carries a new fact, fold the fact into the sentence before.
no-tidy-paragraph-endings.when_to_keep: Keep a closing sentence that makes a genuine turn in the argument.

editor_guidance.why: Paragraphs close with miniature conclusions or neat handovers, tidying where prose should just move on.
editor_guidance.fix: Cut the closing summary; if it carries a new fact, fold the fact into the sentence before.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep a closing sentence that makes a genuine turn in the argument.

editor_action_policy.reason: A less tidy ending must follow the paragraph's actual evidence.

no-title-case-headings.description: Headings with minor words, articles, prepositions, and conjunctions capitalised.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Headings that capitalise every word, down to small ones like `and`, `of`, and `the`. Conventional title case leaves those minor words lowercase; capitalising them is the machine variant.

examples.before: ## Strategic Negotiations And Global Partnerships
examples.after: ## Strategic Negotiations and Global Partnerships

what_it_looks_like.example: ## What We Learned From The Move

no-title-case-headings.how_to_fix: Lowercase the minor words, or recast the heading to match the style of the other headings.

what_it_looks_like.example:
Monday we drove out to the coast road with the boot full of raincoats, and the kids counted tractors until the sea came over the hedge.

Tuesday it rained from breakfast until dark, so we stayed in the cottage and played cards at the kitchen table while the farm dog snored beside the stove.

Wednesday cleared enough for the cliff walk, and the path was muddy the whole way, but we saw seals on the rocks and ate doughnuts by the harbour wall.

Thursday we took the little boat across to the island, where the warden showed the kids the puffin burrows and let them stamp their own tickets.

Friday was market day in the square, and we came back with smoked fish, brown bread, and a wooden spoon nobody would admit to buying.

Saturday the wind came back and flattened the grass, so we flew the kite until the string burned our fingers and then hid in the pub with chowder.

Sunday we packed the car before breakfast, swept the sand out of the hall, left the keys under the flowerpot, and joined the queue of cars heading home.

paragraph-length-uniformity.when_to_keep: Keep even paragraphs in formats that give every entry equal space by design: reference entries, FAQ answers, release notes. The check still flags them.

editor_guidance.fix: Let each paragraph run the length its point needs: split one, cut one to a line, or merge two.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep even paragraphs where the format gives entries equal space: reference entries, FAQ answers.

editor_action_policy.reason: Paragraph splitting or merging depends on idea structure.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Sentence after sentence lands at about the same length, so the piece keeps one flat rhythm from start to finish. G12 covers uniform paragraph lengths; this pattern covers uniform sentence lengths.

what_it_looks_like.prose: Every concept gets a new word each time it appears, and nothing is called the same thing twice. People repeat the words that matter; machine writing swaps in synonyms.

examples.before: Modern enterprises confront unprecedented complexity: sprawling supply chains, volatile markets, evolving regulations, and shifting consumer expectations. Legacy infrastructure strains beneath mounting transactional volume while nimble startups exploit emerging niches. Digital transformation promises salvation yet demands substantial investment, organisational realignment, and cultural adaptation. Executives juggle competing priorities, balancing immediate profitability against durable resilience. Cloud migration accelerates innovation cycles, artificial intelligence augments human judgment, and automation streamlines repetitive workflows. Meanwhile cybersecurity threats proliferate, regulatory scrutiny intensifies, and talent shortages persist. Successful leaders cultivate adaptive mindsets, empowering distributed teams and embracing disciplined experimentation. They articulate compelling visions, communicate transparently, and measure relentlessly. Ultimately competitive advantage flows toward organisations that blend technological sophistication with genuine empathy, converting disruption into opportunity.
examples.after: Most companies today face the same problem: their markets move faster than their systems. The old systems were built for a slower market, and the people who run them know it. Moving to newer systems costs money and takes time, and the move only pays off if the people who use the systems every day actually change how they work. The companies that get through it are the ones that pick one problem, fix that problem, and then move to the next one. The work is slow and the work is dull, but slow, dull work is what change looks like from the inside.

what_it_looks_like.example: The house sits at the end of Weaver Lane, and the property has been empty since March. The vendor wants a quick sale, but the residence needs rewiring before any bank will lend against the dwelling. Prospective buyers toured the home on Saturday; several purchasers returned Sunday with builders, and one bidder brought an architect. The seller refused the first offer, judging the proposal too low, and rejected a second tender within hours. Meanwhile the abode gathers leaves, the garden grows wild, foxes den under the porch, and damp climbs the kitchen wall. Neighbours watch the building decay and wonder whether the owner will ever accept that the place is worth less each passing month.

editor_guidance.fix: Reuse the word you already gave the thing instead of a synonym.
editor_guidance.keep: Keep the variety when each new word names a genuinely new thing rather than restating an old one.
